prerequisites: Applied Mathematics I: Integral and differential calculus. Differential equations.
Applied Mathematics II: Matrix calculus. Solving systems of equations.
Physics I: Vectors, Kinematics and Dynamics.

learning_outcomes.text: Acquire knowledge to apply the basic principles of Mechanics in engineering problems, particularly in the analysis of mechanisms.
Understanding and interpretation of texts and data, development of skills for their concretization and clear and concise exposition.
Aptitude for the distribution of resources and time and their implementation in real situations.
Ability to use scientific-technical tools for solving calculation and design problems in Industrial Engineering and aptitude for seeking sustainable engineering solutions.
Ability for collaborative work and ability to develop multidisciplinary projects.
Knowledge and mastery of the basic concepts on the general laws of mechanics in mechanical engineering.

syllabus_topics: Introduction: Previous notions: Vector systems. Reference systems. Vector function of scalar variable. Boure's rule.
Kinematics of a Material Point: Trajectory. Velocity. Acceleration. Intrinsic components. Rectilinear motion. Curvilinear motion.
Kinematics of a Rigid Body: Concept of rigid body. Velocity field. Acceleration field. Translational motion. Rotational motion. Motion with a fixed point. Planar motion.

Motion with Respect to Multiple Reference Systems: Velocity and acceleration of a material point with respect to different reference systems. Motion of a rigid body with respect to different reference systems. Composition of motions. Theorem of the three centers.
Complements of Statics: Centers of gravity. Moments and Products of inertia. Friction forces.

Dynamics of a Material Point: Fundamental Principles. Inertial reference systems. Work. Power. Conservative forces. Potential Energy. Theorems of the Dynamics of a material point. Dynamics in non-inertial reference systems.

Dynamics of a Rigid Body: Fundamental concepts of the Dynamics of Material Systems. Adaptation of the principles of Point Dynamics to System Dynamics. Theorems of System Dynamics. Dynamics of rigid material systems with planar motion. Dynamics of a rigid material system with rotational motion. Static and Dynamic Balancing of Machines. Application of the Angular Momentum Theorem. Introduction to the study of the Gyroscope.

assessment_methods.method: Theoretical knowledge tests of the subject
Practical knowledge tests of the subject
